svg.aria-label: How to write 离: 10 strokes · 9 pen lifts · 10 movements
svg.title: Writing 离
svg.desc: 10 frames; frame N shows movements 1 to N of 离 (chinese), the movement being added drawn in ink over the finished letter, whose outline is read from _fonts/NotoSansSC-Subset.ttf. Stroke order after Hanzi Writer Data 离.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–10 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chanind/hanzi-writer-data/68d10a4b21150cae5e1ebbd223eed289cf32d90c/data/%E7%A6%BB.json>. Source note on variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies ten ordered strokes for 离, in three pieces. Medians 1–2 draw a dot and a horizontal on top. Medians 3–6 draw the middle: a short left-falling stroke and a dot crossing it, then a box open at the top (a vertical that turns right along its foot without lifting, and a short vertical on the right). Medians 7–10 draw the foot: the frame's left side, a horizontal that turns down the right side and hooks to the left without lifting, then inside it a stroke that falls to the left and turns right without lifting, and a dot. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those ten ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turns, the hook and nine intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.
